card.name: Words just before an outcome or effect
card.fires_on: Small words or modifiers right before a result noun like efficacy, response rates or benefit, after phrases like 'resulted in' or 'did not demonstrate'. Also the space after 'every' in dosing schedules.

modes.label: Before an effect noun
modes.description: Word like greater, increased or the that comes after 'resulted in' or 'did not demonstrate' and before efficacy, benefit or mortality.
modes.example: subjects weighing more than 100 kg, 45 mg was also shown to be efficacious. However, 90 mg resulted in<< greater>> efficacy in these subjects [see Clinical Studies

modes.label: Inside response-rate terms
modes.description: Partway through the abbreviation ACR before 'response rates' in combination-therapy comparisons.
modes.example: with Enbrel alone (0%) [see Warnings and Precautions (5.12) ] and did not result in higher A<<CR>> response rates compared to Enbrel alone

modes.label: Dosing interval gap
modes.description: The space after 'every' in a dosing schedule.
modes.example: Psoriatic Arthritis: Adults: 150 mg administered by subcutaneous injection at Week 0, Week 4, and every<< >>

card.writes: It pushes words meaning exhibits, expression and showing an effect, so the text goes on to name an outcome.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence is about to say what effect or result a drug showed.
